m.n: Sources of Authority: Scripture, Tradition & Magisterium

co.n: Sources of Authority: Scripture, Tradition & Magisterium Cohort

c.p: What is the "Tripod of Truth" in Catholic theology that authentically conveys divine revelation?
c.a: sacred scripture, sacred tradition, and the magisterium | scripture tradition magisterium | bible tradition and magisterium
c.h: Three interdependent pillars; none can stand alone without the other two.
c.e: According to Dei Verbum, Sacred Scripture and Sacred Tradition form one sacred deposit of the Word of God, interpreted by the living Magisterium; none can exist without the others (CCC 84–95).
r: scripture alone (sola scriptura) with personal private interpretation
Catholic teaching emphasizes that Sacred Scripture was written and recognized within the living Tradition of the Church and requires the Magisterium for authentic interpretation.

c.p: What is the Magisterium of the Catholic Church?
c.a: the living teaching authority of the church exercised by the pope and bishops in communion with him | teaching office of the pope and bishops | teaching authority of the church
c.h: Guided by the Holy Spirit to safeguard, interpret, and defend the apostolic deposit of faith.
c.e: The Magisterium is the living teaching office of the Church, exercised by the successor of Peter (the Pope) and the bishops united with him, to preserve Christian doctrine from error (CCC 85–88).
r: political assembly that rewrites the bible each year
The Magisterium does not invent new revelation; it faithfully preserves, defends, and expounds the deposit of faith entrusted by Christ once and for all.
